proof_summary: A finite cotangent Fourier identity expresses the difference between the sum of negative quadratic residues and the original residue sum as a divisor sum of cotangent-weighted imaginary parts of quadratic Gauss sums. Explicit Gauss-sum evaluations reduce every local term to a nonnegative multiple of an odd character cotangent sum—whose nonnegativity follows from the positive Euler product for its Dirichlet series and the cotangent partial-fraction limit—and comparison with the mirror sum then gives the bound.
